correctness.rationale: For each tuple of up to three nonzero singular vectors, Witt extension reduces orbit data to linear-dependency coordinates and an alternating Gram matrix. The exactly derived quadratic Fourier sum counts every candidate extension, including zero, which is correctly removed; outside-span realizations and repeated vertices are handled separately. For r>=5 the explicit lower bound is greater than the entire selected span, proving universal extension patterns for every sign. A finite complete recursion over every allowed one-point extension certifies four root rank-four signatures at r=2,3,4,5, and direct enumeration independently checks all the small-model orbit extensions and witness properties for both signs at r=2,3,4. Finite computations are not used for the infinite bound; rank-four truth and sharp representatives follow from the resulting four classes.

value.rationale: A natural pair of infinite orthogonal polar-geometry families has a complete, sharp logical description using only depth four in the pure point-collinearity graph. The nontrivial distinction between rank-three hyperbolic and elliptic quadrics and the 35-point common representative capture what low-depth first-order logic can detect about Arf sign and Witt index. Edge, claw and four-clique predicates give a depth-preserving normal form on this family, so the exact classification has mathematical interpretation beyond the computed finite orbit census.
